hypotheses.title: Operator Precedence Bug in createPool Deposit Validation Allows Zero-Liquidity Pools and Blocks Token1-Only Deposits
hypotheses.mechanism: At ModuleLiquidity.sol:90, the deposit validation check `if (deposit0 | deposit1 == 0)` suffers from Solidity operator precedence: the equality operator `==` (precedence 10) binds tighter than bitwise OR `|` (precedence 12), so the expression evaluates as `deposit0 | (deposit1 == 0)` instead of the intended `(deposit0 | deposit1) == 0`. Truth table analysis: (1) deposit0=0, deposit1=0: evaluates to `0 | (0==0)` = `0 | true` = `0 | 1` = 1 (truthy) → revert NOT triggered → ZERO deposits accepted. (2) deposit0=0, deposit1>0: evaluates to `0 | (X==0)` = `0 | false` = `0 | 0` = 0 (falsy) → revert IS triggered → valid token1-only deposits BLOCKED. (3) deposit0>0, deposit1=0: evaluates to `X | (0==0)` = `X | 1` = non-zero → revert NOT triggered → asymmetric acceptance of token0-only. Cross-referenced with SingleProviderPoolType.addLiquidity (lines 180-205) which returns user-specified amount0/amount1 without requiring both non-zero, confirming single-sided deposits are a valid pool type feature. The reserves at line 88-89 are read from `ptrPoolState` which points to the NEWLY CREATED pool, so the bug allows pools to be 'created with liquidity' while having zero reserves.
grounded_in: code-observation: Solidity operator precedence table — `==` (precedence 10) binds tighter than `|` (precedence 12), causing `a | b == 0` to parse as `a | (b == 0)` not `(a | b) == 0`. The boolean result of `b == 0` is implicitly cast to uint256 (0 or 1) before the bitwise OR.

code-observation: SingleProviderPoolType.addLiquidity (lines 180-205) returns user-specified amount0/amount1 directly without requiring both to be non-zero, confirming single-sided deposits are a valid pool type feature that triggers the bug.

code-observation: ModuleLiquidity.sol:88-89 reads reserves from `Storage.appStorage().pools[poolId]` where `poolId` is the NEWLY created pool from line 75, meaning the reserves reflect only what the delegatecalled addLiquidity deposited.
Pattern 1: Arithmetic precision errors — operator precedence is a subcategory of arithmetic correctness issues that cause logic to diverge from intent

coupled_pair.state_a: Intended check: (deposit0 | deposit1) == 0 — true only when BOTH deposits are zero
coupled_pair.state_b: Actual check: deposit0 | (deposit1 == 0) — true when deposit0 is non-zero OR deposit1 is zero (completely different semantics)
coupled_pair.invariant: createPool with liquidityData must revert when the resulting deposits are both zero

masking_code.masks_invariant: The bug is masked in the common case where both deposit0 > 0 AND deposit1 > 0, since `nonzero | (nonzero == 0)` = `nonzero | 0` = nonzero (correctly passes). It only manifests for edge cases: zero-only deposits (should revert, doesn't) and single-sided token1 deposits (should pass, reverts).

hypotheses.title: Division-by-Zero DoS in Shortage Calculation When poolFeeBPS and lpFeeBPS Are Both MAX_BPS
hypotheses.mechanism: In _applySwapByInputInputFees at AMMModule.sol:2657-2660, the shortage calculation uses FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp(shortage, DOUBLE_BPS, denominator) where denominator = `DOUBLE_BPS - uint256(poolFeeBPS) * uint256(swapCache.protocolFeeStructure.lpFeeBPS)`. When poolFeeBPS == MAX_BPS (10000) and lpFeeBPS == MAX_BPS (10000), the denominator becomes `100_000_000 - 10000 * 10000 = 0`. FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp delegates to mulDiv which at FullMath.sol:52 checks `if (denominator <= prod1)` — when denominator is 0, this is `0 <= 0` = true, causing a revert with FullMath__MulDivOverflowError(). Both conditions can coexist: (1) poolFeeBPS == MAX_BPS is allowed for input swaps via dynamic pool fee hooks — _getPoolFee at AMMModule.sol:1717 checks `poolFeeBPS > MAX_BPS` (strict greater-than) for input swaps, allowing exactly MAX_BPS=10000. (2) lpFeeBPS == MAX_BPS is allowed by _setProtocolFees at AMMModule.sol:3459 which checks `lpFeeBPS > MAX_BPS` (strict greater-than). The shortage path at line 2652 is entered when `protocolFeeFromHookFees + expectedProtocolLPFee < minimumProtocolFee`, which occurs when hop fees set a minimum that hook fee contributions don't fully satisfy.
grounded_in: code-observation: _getPoolFee at AMMModule.sol:1717 uses `poolFeeBPS > MAX_BPS` (strict >) for input swaps, allowing exactly MAX_BPS (10000). This is an intentional asymmetry — output swaps use `poolFeeBPS >= MAX_BPS` (rejecting MAX_BPS).
code-observation: _setProtocolFees at AMMModule.sol:3459 uses `lpFeeBPS > MAX_BPS` (strict >), allowing exactly MAX_BPS (10000) as a valid LP protocol fee.
code-observation: DOUBLE_BPS = MAX_BPS * MAX_BPS = 100_000_000 at Constants.sol:79. Denominator = 100_000_000 - 10000 * 10000 = 0.
code-observation: FullMath.mulDiv at FullMath.sol:52 — `if (denominator <= prod1)` catches denominator=0 since 0 <= 0 is true, reverting with FullMath__MulDivOverflowError().

coupled_pair.state_a: poolFeeBPS = MAX_BPS (allowed for input swaps by _getPoolFee line 1717 strict > check)
coupled_pair.state_b: lpFeeBPS = MAX_BPS (allowed by _setProtocolFees line 3459 strict > check)
coupled_pair.invariant: The denominator DOUBLE_BPS - poolFeeBPS * lpFeeBPS must be positive for the shortage calculation to succeed

masking_code.masks_invariant: The shortage path at line 2652 is only entered under specific fee conditions (hook fees + LP fees insufficient to cover hop fee minimum). Most pools never enter this path, masking the division-by-zero. Additionally, dynamic fee pools are rare, and lpFeeBPS is typically set well below MAX_BPS.

hypotheses.title: Queued Hook Fee Execution Clears Reentrancy Flags — Creates Unguarded Re-entry Window via Token Callbacks
hypotheses.mechanism: In _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers (AMMModule.sol:3183-3204), line 3190 calls _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS). Per TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol:68-72, _setReentrancyFlags strips ENTERED and NOT_ENTERED bits from `flags` (yielding 0) then preserves only the ENTERED bit from current state: `currentGuard = _getTstorish(...) & ENTERED` → stores `ENTERED | 0 = ENTERED (0x02)`. All operation-specific flags (SWAP_GUARD_FLAG=0x04, LIQUIDITY_GUARD_FLAG=0x80, FLASHLOAN_GUARD_FLAG=0x800) are CLEARED. The function then iterates queued transfers (lines 3192-3201), each calling _transferHookFeesByHook which performs SafeERC20.safeTransfer at line 3133. If the fee token implements transfer callbacks (ERC-777 tokensReceived), the recipient contract gains execution. The recipient calls collectHookFeesByHook (ModuleFeeCollection.sol:72). The check at line 75 tests _isReentrancyFlagSet(SWAP_GUARD_FLAG) — returns FALSE (flag cleared). Line 77 tests FLASHLOAN_GUARD_FLAG — also FALSE. Execution falls through to line 80: _transferHookFeesByHook(msg.sender, ...) — DIRECT execution, bypassing the intended queueing mechanism. A hook collecting fees for the SAME hookFeeKey in the callback drains the tokensOwed balance via the direct path. When the loop continues to process remaining queue entries for the same key, _transferHookFeesByHook finds insufficient balance — underflow check at line 3130 triggers revert. Since executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers was called via external CALL at line 2247, the revert propagates to _finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse, bricking the entire swap.
grounded_in: code-observation: _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) at AMMModule.sol:3190 — per TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol:69 `flags = flags & ~(ENTERED | NOT_ENTERED)` yields 0, line 70 extracts ENTERED from current, line 71 stores `ENTERED | 0 = ENTERED`. SWAP_GUARD_FLAG (1<<2=4) is NOT in result. _isReentrancyFlagSet(4) at ModuleFeeCollection.sol:75 returns (2 & 4 > 0) = false.

code-observation: collectHookFeesByHook at ModuleFeeCollection.sol:72-82 has NO nonReentrant modifier — it relies on flag-specific checks (SWAP_GUARD_FLAG, LIQUIDITY_GUARD_FLAG, FLASHLOAN_GUARD_FLAG) which are all cleared, causing fall-through to direct _transferHookFeesByHook at line 80.

EXP-9: Read-only reentrancy pattern variant — state (tokensOwed) is committed before the re-entry opportunity. The queued entries reference committed state that the callback can access and modify through the unguarded collectHookFeesByHook path.
Solodit: Bunni v2 reentrancy lock bypass (Cyfrin audit) — BunniHub.unlockForRebalance() cleared reentrancy protection during hook execution, allowing hooks to re-enter via token callbacks.

coupled_pair.state_a: Reentrancy flags in transient storage — cleared to ENTERED-only at AMMModule.sol:3190
coupled_pair.state_b: tokensOwed[hookFeeKey] in persistent storage — decremented by both queue loop (line 3129) and direct collectHookFeesByHook (same line via callback)
coupled_pair.invariant: Swap-specific reentrancy flags must remain set while AMM state is being mutated during fee distribution

masking_code.masks_invariant: executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers msg.sender==address(this) check (line 128) prevents DIRECT external calls but does not prevent re-entry through token transfer callbacks during the flag-cleared window. The ENTERED bit blocks core operations (swap/addLiquidity/removeLiquidity) but not collectHookFeesByHook which uses flag-based access control.

hypotheses.title: Unchecked Hook Fee Addition Overflow Corrupts Pool Fee Hook Amount Input
hypotheses.mechanism: In _executePoolFeeHook at AMMModule.sol:1752-1757, the unchecked block computes `uint256 totalHookFees = swapCache.tokenInTokenInFee + swapCache.tokenOutTokenInFee` and then `amount -= totalHookFees`. Both the addition and subtraction are unchecked. The hook fee values are set by external token hook contracts via _executeSwapHook (line 2522: `feeAmount := mload(0x00)`) with NO validation on the returned uint256 value — the return is simply loaded from memory with no bounds check. If two malicious token hooks return values that sum to more than type(uint256).max, the addition overflows. The resulting incorrect `totalHookFees` is subtracted from `amount` (also unchecked), producing a corrupted value. This corrupted `amount` is passed to the pool fee hook at line 1771 as the swap amount parameter via `mstore(add(hookMemoryPointer, 0x200), amount)`. The pool fee hook uses this amount to determine the dynamic fee rate (poolFeeBPS). The comment at line 1755 states 'Underflow will be checked in _applySwapByInputInputFees', but that function only validates individual fee values against swapAmountIn (lines 2616, 2629), NOT their overflowed sum.
grounded_in: code-observation: _executeSwapHook at AMMModule.sol:2522 returns hook fee via `feeAmount := mload(0x00)` with no bounds check on the returned uint256 — any value the hook returns is accepted
code-observation: The unchecked block at AMMModule.sol:1752-1757 performs both addition (line 1754) and subtraction (line 1756) without overflow/underflow protection
code-observation: _applySwapByInputInputFees validates individual fees at lines 2616 (`feeAmount > swapAmountIn`) and 2629 (same), but does NOT validate their sum, which is where the overflow occurs
EXP-13: Arbitrary external call data manipulation — malicious hooks return crafted values to corrupt internal calculations passed to the pool fee hook

coupled_pair.state_a: swapCache.tokenInTokenInFee and swapCache.tokenOutTokenInFee — unbounded uint256 values from external token hooks
coupled_pair.state_b: amount parameter passed to pool fee hook — should represent actual swap amount available for fee calculation
coupled_pair.invariant: The amount passed to the pool fee hook must accurately reflect the swap amount after legitimate fee deductions, not an overflowed/underflowed artifact

masking_code.masks_invariant: Comment 'Underflow will be checked in _applySwapByInputInputFees' creates false assurance that downstream validation catches all issues. The downstream checks validate INDIVIDUAL fee values, not the overflowed SUM that corrupted the pool fee hook's input.

hypotheses.title: Output Swap Partial Fill Stores Irrevocable Hook Fees for Non-Actualized Volume
hypotheses.mechanism: In _poolSwapByOutput (AMMModule.sol), _applySwapByOutputOutputFees is called at line 1537 BEFORE the pool type's swapByOutput call at line 1548. Inside _applySwapByOutputOutputFees (lines 2851-2895): tokenInTokenOutFee and tokenOutTokenOutFee (set by beforeSwapHooks) are ADDED to swapAmountOut (lines 2863, 2875), increasing the amount the pool must provide. These hook fees are irrevocably committed to persistent storage via _storeHookFees at lines 2871 and 2887. The inflated amountOut is passed to the pool type. If the pool type returns actualAmountOut < originalAmountOut (partial fill, line 1559), the adjustment at lines 1569-1582 reduces adjustedAmountSpecified (user's output) by amountOutAdjustment = originalAmountOut - actualAmountOut (line 1569). The stored hook fees are NOT proportionally reduced. In contrast, input swap partial fills at lines 1413-1427 explicitly adjust exchange fees (line 1420: exchangeFeeAdjustment = mulDiv(...)) and protocol fees (line 1421). This asymmetry means the ENTIRE shortfall from partial fill is absorbed by the user while hooks receive 100% of their pre-fill fees.
grounded_in: code-observation: _storeHookFees at lines 2871/2887 writes to persistent storage (tokensOwed mapping via AMMModule.sol:2988) inside _applySwapByOutputOutputFees (line 1537), which executes BEFORE the pool type call at line 1548. Once written, there is no mechanism to decrement or reverse these entries.

code-observation: Input swap partial fill adjustment (lines 1413-1427) proportionally adjusts exchangeFeeAmount (line 1425) and protocolFeeFromFees (line 1426) using mulDiv ratio. Output swap partial fill (lines 1569-1582) adjusts ONLY adjustedAmountSpecified and amountOut — no analogous hook fee adjustment exists.

EXP-9: State committed before completion — hook fees are committed to persistent storage before the pool type determines actual execution, analogous to read-only reentrancy where committed state is observed before final validation.
code-observation: SingleProviderPoolType can partial fill by design (verified at AMMModule.sol line 1565: only first hop can partial fill)

coupled_pair.state_a: tokensOwed[hookFeeKey] — committed at lines 2871/2887 based on ORIGINAL amountOut before pool type call
coupled_pair.state_b: swapCache.amountOut — reduced by partial fill at line 1577 to actualAmountOut after pool type call
coupled_pair.invariant: Hook fees committed to storage must correspond to the actual trade volume after partial fill adjustment

masking_code.masks_invariant: Partial fill check at line 1572 prevents amountOutAdjustment from exceeding adjustedAmountSpecified but does NOT check or adjust the irrevocable hook fees stored 40 lines earlier

hypotheses.title: Flash Loan Fee Basis Override — Token Hook Returns tokenFeeAmount=1 to Near-Eliminate Flash Loan Costs
hypotheses.mechanism: In _flashLoan (AMMModule.sol:3288-3382), the fee calculation at lines 3298-3303 has two paths: (1) When tokenFeeAmount == 0 (no hook fee): feeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(loanAmount, flashLoanBPS, MAX_BPS) — fee is proportional to LOAN AMOUNT. (2) When tokenFeeAmount > 0 (hook sets a fee): feeAmount = tokenFeeAmount + mulDivRoundingUp(tokenFeeAmount, flashLoanBPS, MAX_BPS) — fee is proportional to HOOK'S FEE AMOUNT, not loan amount. In path (2), the protocol's flashLoanBPS is applied as a percentage of the hook's fee, not the loan. If a token hook returns tokenFeeAmount=1 (1 wei), then feeAmount = 1 + ceil(1 * flashLoanBPS / 10000) = 1 + 1 = 2 wei (for any flashLoanBPS > 0). For a 1,000,000 token loan with flashLoanBPS=30 (0.3%): path (1) would charge 3000 tokens; path (2) charges 2 wei. Protocol fee at line 3378: _storeProtocolFees(feeToken, feeAmount - tokenFeeAmount) = _storeProtocolFees(feeToken, 1 wei). A token owner deploys a hook that returns tokenFeeAmount=1 for flash loans (enabled via TOKEN_SETTINGS_FLASHLOANS_FLAG). All flash loans of that token pay ~1 wei instead of the intended percentage-based fee.
grounded_in: code-observation: Conditional at AMMModule.sol:3299 switches fee computation basis. Path tokenFeeAmount==0 at line 3300 uses `loanAmount` as base. Path tokenFeeAmount>0 at line 3302 uses `tokenFeeAmount` as base. For loanAmount=1e18, flashLoanBPS=30, tokenFeeAmount=1: path1 yields 3e14, path2 yields 2.

code-observation: Token hooks are set by token owners via setTokenSettings (ModuleAdmin.sol:272). The TOKEN_SETTINGS_FLASHLOANS_FLAG enables the flash loan hook. The hook's returned tokenFeeAmount has no minimum bound.

EXP-14: Diamond proxy extension hijacker — the token hook system allows token owners to override core protocol fee logic. The fee calculation delegates to the hook, which can return a value that nullifies the protocol's intended fee structure.

coupled_pair.state_a: flashLoanBPS (protocol-set fee rate, intended to apply proportionally to loanAmount)
coupled_pair.state_b: tokenFeeAmount (hook-returned value that becomes the new fee basis when > 0)
coupled_pair.invariant: Protocol flash loan fee should be proportional to the loan amount, not substitutable by a hook returning an arbitrary (possibly minimal) value

masking_code.masks_invariant: The expression `tokenFeeAmount + mulDivRoundingUp(tokenFeeAmount, flashLoanBPS, MAX_BPS)` appears to add protocol fee ON TOP of hook fee, masking that the protocol fee base changed from loanAmount to tokenFeeAmount

hypotheses.title: createPool Clears Reentrancy Guard Before User-Controlled Delegatecall, Enabling Unguarded Intermediate State
hypotheses.mechanism: In createPool at ModuleLiquidity.sol:79-81, the function explicitly calls `_clearReentrancyGuard()` before performing `address(this).delegatecall(liquidityData)`. _clearReentrancyGuard calls _nonReentrantAfter (TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol:64-66, 88-90), which sets the transient storage guard to NOT_ENTERED (0x01). This completely drops reentrancy protection — the ENTERED bit (0x02) is NOT set. The delegatecall at line 81 goes through the diamond proxy's fallback dispatcher. During dispatch routing and before addLiquidity's nonReentrantWithFlags modifier executes, the guard is NOT_ENTERED. If the proxy's dispatch logic or any pre-execution hook checks reentrancy state during this window, they see an unguarded state. Furthermore, createPool's own nonReentrant modifier's _nonReentrantAfter cleanup (which runs after the delegatecall returns) sets the guard to NOT_ENTERED again — a no-op since addLiquidity's own cleanup already reset it. This means the outer nonReentrant modifier provides no protection for the code after the delegatecall returns. Combined with the operator precedence bug (H-DP-01), a crafted liquidityData can target a different pool, and the zero-deposit validation passes incorrectly.
grounded_in: EXP-14: Diamond proxy selector collision and dispatch patterns — the delegatecall through the proxy creates a trust boundary crossing where guard state matters for dispatch-level security checks
code-observation: TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol:64-66 — _clearReentrancyGuard calls _nonReentrantAfter which sets guard to NOT_ENTERED (0x01), fully clearing the ENTERED bit

code-observation: The delegatecall at ModuleLiquidity.sol:81 uses user-controlled liquidityData — only the 4-byte selector (line 78) is validated, the remaining calldata (poolId, amounts, etc.) is arbitrary
code-observation: The outer nonReentrant modifier's _nonReentrantAfter at ModuleLiquidity.sol:74 becomes a no-op since the inner addLiquidity already reset to NOT_ENTERED

coupled_pair.state_a: Reentrancy guard after _clearReentrancyGuard() — NOT_ENTERED (0x01), no protection
coupled_pair.state_b: User-controlled liquidityData determining target pool and amounts in delegatecall
coupled_pair.invariant: Reentrancy protection should be continuously enforced during pool creation, including any nested delegatecalls

masking_code.masks_invariant: The selector check `bytes4(liquidityData[0:4]) == this.addLiquidity.selector` at line 78 restricts the delegatecall to addLiquidity, which re-establishes the guard via its own modifier. But the guard is down between lines 79-81, and the user controls the parameters (poolId, amounts) in liquidityData, allowing the delegatecall to target arbitrary pools.
